changes: Purpose reworded: 'liṣiti manajasyārthena' may name a beneficiary (a person called Manaja or similar) rather than 'mankind'; flagged as uncertain, no person added
Notes expanded: ambiguity of manajasyārthena; date check NS 541 + 880 = 1421 (Vaiśākha falls in April–May 1421); no scribe named

purpose: for the sake of 'manaja' (liṣiti manajasyārthena): either manujasyārthena, 'for another person / for people', or a beneficiary's name; unclear
notes: The colophon names no scribe, commissioner or owner. 'aṃgaḍa(!)kumārakīyeḥ(?)' is part of the section title (Aṅgada, an epic character), not a person. 'liṣiti manajasyārthena' is probably 'likhitaṃ manujasyārthena'. The formula 'likhitaṃ X-sya arthena' usually takes the name of the person the copy was made for, so 'Manaja' (or something like Maṇija or Manuja) could be a corrupt personal name. It has been left out of the person list because the reading is too uncertain. Era not stated: the catalogue reads it as NS, which fits the Newari script, giving 1421 CE. The month is Vaiśākha (kṛṣṇa tṛtīyā), around April–May 1421. 'thathatha thathaḥ' is a filler or closing flourish.
